clue.text: Pastime in craft circle, cutting leaves

indicators.note: something cutting into a word slices into its middle, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A hobby taken up in a crafting circle, involving trimming foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests handicrafts, but here it means a ship: deck quoits is a classic game played on cruise liners.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits, ring-tossing at a peg, is the traditional deck game on passenger ships, a shipboard pastime.

clue.text: Disorder in leisure club mounted

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, straddling the gap
in a down clue, mounted means climbing upward, so the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: the letters running across the end of leisure and start of club

explanation.surface: Some kind of trouble has broken out at a sports and leisure club.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is a sore, a medical complaint, and disorder is used in the sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Head of Institute dropping academic dinosaur

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: The director of an institute is losing an academic, apparently a fossil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: the excrement of seabirds.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur of the Cretaceous period.

clue.text: Problem around Asian peak once held up by British mountain buff?

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps the other pieces in this clue
in a down clue, being held up by something means sitting directly on top of it

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
K1 was the survey label for Masherbrum in the Karakoram, the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A Himalayan summit question sits on top of a British climbing enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: Masherbrum's old survey name K1 parallels the better-known K2; in a down clue, being held up by something means sitting above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski bum is someone who lives for skiing, a slope enthusiast; the question mark flags the loose sense of buff.

clue.text: Tree boundary around fort put back building work

indicators.note: around says the boundary word encloses the next piece
putting something back here means turning it round end to end

blocks.note: in cricket, a boundary is a hit worth six runs
Ft is the abbreviation for fort, as in Fort William

explanation.surface: A tree line around a fort has been put back on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: A boundary in cricket is a shot reaching the rope; clearing it scores six.
explanation.definitionFit: First fix is the stage of construction where pipes and wiring are run before walls are plastered.

clue.text: Profitable Spanish artist barely drawing picture

indicators.note: barely suggests stripping something bare, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: a fat contract is a lucrative one

explanation.surface: A lucrative Spanish painter is only just managing to sketch an image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' and 'picture' look like art terms; picture means a film, and drawing means pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal Attraction is the 1987 thriller film, and a picture is a movie.

clue.text: Track free holiday without thanks

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following word is taken out

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Getting a free holiday without even saying thank you leaves people on the wrong track.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ridgeway is an ancient trackway across southern England, now a National Trail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ridgeway is a named long-distance path, so a track in the sense of a route on foot.

clue.text: Once noble isle in the main

indicators.note: in the main means for the most part, so most of the word is kept and its end dropped

blocks.note: the Isle of Thanet in Kent, once separated from the mainland

explanation.surface: A former aristocrat lives on an island in the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' suggests the sea, but it means mostly. THANET is a district of Kent, England, still called an isle.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a landholding lord in Anglo-Saxon England and Scotland, a historical rank of nobility.

clue.text: Mad, topless ascetic maybe entering varying states

indicators.note: topless means missing the top, which in a down clue is the first letter
entering means going inside the following pair of words

blocks.note: two different US states by abbreviation: Ill. (Illinois) and Cal. (California)
a yogi is an example of an ascetic, hence maybe

explanation.surface: A semi-naked holy man wanders through various states, apparently crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The beheaded YOGI goes between the two state abbreviations ILL and CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogical means irrational or senseless, which is one sense of mad.

clue.text: Familiar tone embodying clubs favoured rocker

indicators.note: to embody something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: aqua is a shade or tone of blue-green
a Teddy boy, a 1950s rock'n'roll fan

explanation.surface: A familiar sound comes from a much-loved rock star holding a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' suggests a musician, but it means a Teddy boy, the British 1950s youth subculture.
explanation.definitionFit: To be acquainted with something is to know it, to be familiar with it.

clue.text: Rod Laver's opening penetrating chop

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
penetrating means getting inside the following word

explanation.surface: Tennis great Rod Laver's opening shot cuts through a chop.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Laver, the Australian tennis champion, makes 'Rod' look like a first name rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or shaft on which wheels turn.

clue.text: Organised bed covering, on rotation still

indicators.note: rotating the word moves its last letter round to the front
covering means the bed word wraps around the first word

blocks.note: a quilt is a bed covering

explanation.surface: A neatly arranged duvet, put in a rota, keeps everything calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotation moves the bed word's final letter to its front before the organised piece slips in; 'still' is an adjective, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranquil means calm and undisturbed, the adjectival sense of still.

clue.text: Runner faces track after putting in good amount of work

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside the track word
one thing facing another stands in front of it in the line

blocks.note: the River Exe in Devon; rivers run

explanation.surface: An athlete stands facing the track after a good deal of training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a crossword staple for a river; here the Exe of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: In thermodynamics, exergy is the maximum useful work obtainable from a system.

clue.text: Surrounded by morning papers

explanation.surface: Someone at breakfast is buried under the morning newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morning papers' looks like the dailies, but the papers are identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid is a preposition meaning in the middle of or among things.

clue.text: Mother catches prime youth with September's centre spread

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside
the centre of a nine-letter word is its fifth letter

blocks.note: to prime a weapon is to arm it

explanation.surface: A mother catches her son in his prime in mid-September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime youth' reads as one phrase, but prime is a verb meaning load a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve spread on toast.

clue.text: Reporter's searched thoroughly following tense conduct

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the words, so the letters are what the word sounds like
following means coming after, so the searched piece is placed second behind the tense piece

explanation.surface: A journalist turned the place upside down after a tense stand-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to carry it out, which is the verb conduct.

clue.text: Store most important bric-a-brac in residence northwards

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces inside the residence word
in a down clue, going north means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: number one, written NO 1, the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their finest knick-knacks at their northern home.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(NOI TAT)S goes upward. 'Store' looks like a verb but is a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a shop selling paper and pens, so a store.

clue.text: Soldier, with regular chaps keeping in charge, makes merry

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within

explanation.surface: A soldier celebrates with his ordinary mates and their commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to celebrate joyfully, which is what making merry means.

clue.text: Relative regretted rejecting lofty property

indicators.note: rejecting means throwing back, so the word is turned round

explanation.surface: A family member regrets turning down a grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lofty property' suggests a building, but property means quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is the quality of magnificence and loftiness, an attribute or property.

clue.text: Jambalaya occasionally served with skill

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A chef serves the rice dish expertly now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Ably is an adverb meaning competently, in a skilful way.

clue.text: Studying done here affected our country?

blocks.note: the United States, read as us

explanation.surface: A question about whether study has made the nation pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a description: a place where studying is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university or college, where students learn.

clue.text: People from old coffee plantation finally retiring

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word is used
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the string is turned round

explanation.surface: Workers come from an old coffee estate that is finally closing down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navajo are a Native American people of the south-western United States.

clue.text: On-board command involving a leviathan

explanation.surface: A captain gives an order as a whale appears.
explanation.walkthrough: Leviathan is a noun but stands for the adjective describing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a nautical order meaning stop or hold, given aboard a ship.

clue.text: Least balanced type of paving cropped first around base

indicators.note: cropped means cut short, so the last letter goes
around says the first word wraps the next one

blocks.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: The least stable kind of paving got trimmed first around the foundation.
explanation.walkthrough: Base as E comes from mathematics: e is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Craziest is the superlative of crazy, the one least mentally stable.

clue.text: Outwardly sleek golfing area boosted sport

indicators.note: outwardly means only the outside letters are kept
in a down clue, boosted means lifted upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A smart golf course gave a lift to the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeet is a clay-pigeon shooting sport.

clue.text: Chief drama school making daughter Juliet

indicators.note: making one thing into another swaps a letter for its replacement

blocks.note: the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, London

explanation.surface: The head of a drama school turns a daughter into Juliet.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet suggests Shakespeare at drama school, but it is the radio code word for J.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja is an Indian king or prince, a ruler or chief.

clue.text: Our cousin's ringing about tank having run out

indicators.note: run is cricket shorthand R, and having it out means that letter leaves
about means the ringing word goes around the next one

blocks.note: a chime is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A relative is phoning about a tank that has run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our cousin' means a fellow ape: chimpanzees are humanity's closest living relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Chimpanzees are humans' nearest evolutionary relatives, which makes them our cousins.

clue.text: Spray well inside metal shed

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the metal word

blocks.note: so = well, as in well, then

explanation.surface: A hose is spraying away inside a metal garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a noun for the garden hut, but it is a verb meaning get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to discard or throw away, which is the verb shed.

clue.text: What's the betting luxury hotel offers sample of perfume?

blocks.note: SP, starting price, the odds at a race

explanation.surface: A bookie wonders whether a posh hotel gives out free scent testers.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritz is a quick squirt from a spray, as a perfume tester gives.
